en: A Humble Preface to the *Sūtra on the Ten Kings Spoken by the Buddha Concerning Preparing for Life in the Seven Days*, respectfully offered for recitation.
Regarding the *Sūtra on the Seven Days of Preparing for Rebirth in the Pure Land Spoken by King Yama*: I vow to exhort all who have a karmic connection.
One should open the sūtra with the Five Assemblies, enter into the hymns of praise, and recite the name of Amitābha Buddha.
Composed by the Śramaṇa Zàngchuān of Dàshèngcí Monastery in Chéngdū Prefecture. In praise of the *Buddhabhāṣita-yamalarāja-vyākaraṇa-caturparṣad-pūrvasevā-saptadinopapatti-sukhāvatī-sūtra*:
The Buddha spoke the *Sūtra on the Prophecy of King Yama Bestowing [Instruction] upon the Fourfold Assembly for Cultivating Merit in Advance to Be Reborn in the Pure Land after Seven Days*.
In praise, it is said:
When the Tathāgata was about to enter parinirvāṇa, he extensively summoned the celestial spirits and terrestrial deities.
Having bestowed a prophecy upon King Yama, he then transmitted the ritual for preliminary cultivation during the seven days prior to birth.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was at the city of Kuśinagara, on the banks of the river Hiranyavatī, [at the abode of the Mallas].
Between the twin trees, as he was about to enter parinirvāṇa, his entire body emitted light that universally illuminated the great assembly, including all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
the devas, nāgas, and divine kings, the celestial kings, Śakra Devendra, the four great heavenly kings, Mahābrahmā, the asura kings, the various great kings, the son of Yama,
the Lord of the Great Mountains, the Lord of Fate, the Registrar of Life, and the five...
The Great Devas of the Path and the officials and scribes of the hells all assembled and paid homage to the World-Honored One. Standing with palms joined, they praised him, saying:
"At this time, the Buddha extends his radiance to fill the great trichiliocosm, Universally reaching the dragons and ghosts, the assemblies of humans and devas."
The Śakras, Brahmās, and the various devas of the profound and secret assemblies all came together to prostrate before the World-Honored One.
The Buddha addressed the great multitude: "In a future age, the Son of Heaven Yama shall attain Buddhahood;
his name shall be Samantabhadra-rāja Tathāgata, fully endowed with the ten titles. His land shall be pure and adorned with a hundred jewels; the kingdom shall be named Huayan (Flower Adornment)."
The Bodhisattvas fill [the realm], and they praise, saying:

"World-Honored One, today Yama has recorded this; before long he shall come to realize the Buddha-adorned jewel-land, which is eternally pure, and the assembly of Bodhisattvas who practice therein will be vast."

At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying, “World-Honored One, for what causes and conditions does the Prince Yama preside over judgment in the dark realm, and yet, in this very assembly, immediately receive the prediction of his future fruition?
The Buddha said, “In that dark path, he acts as a king for two reasons: first, he is a bodhisattva dwelling in the stage of immovability within inconceivable liberation.”
First, out of a desire to gather and transform sentient beings who suffer extreme pain, he manifests as kings such as Yama. Second,
because many beings who have practiced virtue but violated the precepts fall into the realm of the Yama devas and become great Māra kings, they govern and oversee all ghosts,
adjudicating all offenders within Jambudvīpa for the ten evil deeds and the five heinous crimes, and imprisoning them in dungeons where they undergo suffering day and night.

Suffering! One revolves within it, receiving a body according to karmic retribution, passing from birth to death with fixed certainty. Now, for this Devaputra Yama, the causes and conditions have matured;
therefore, I prophesy that in a future life he shall be named Bao Yuan (Jewel-Perfected) and realize Great Bodhi. You people, whether gods or humans, should not harbor doubt or suspicion.
Thus it was praised: [Verse of Praise]
Increasing compassion, he universally transforms others and displays awe-inspiring spiritual power;
though the cycle of rebirth in the six realms never pauses, he teaches them to weary of suffering and contemplate peace and happiness. Therefore, he manifests in the form of King Yama.
Furthermore, if there are those who produce this sutra, receive, uphold, read, and recite it, after they pass away, they shall not be born in the three miserable realms.
Entering all the great hells, he praised them, saying:

"If a person has faith in the inconceivable Dharma, by copying the sutra text, listening to it, receiving it, and upholding it, they will instantly transcend the three evil realms upon the end of their life;
this body shall forever be spared from entering the Avīci hell."
On the day of one's birth, if one has committed patricide or matricide, violated the precepts of celibacy, or killed pigs, oxen, sheep, chickens, dogs, or venomous snakes—
any such grave offenses that would cause one to enter hell for ten or five kalpas— if one instead creates this sutra or various sacred images, [the retribution shall be averted].
The record is inscribed upon the karma-mirror. King Yama is pleased and decrees that the person be released. They shall be reborn into a wealthy and noble family, freed from their transgressions.
He praises them, saying:
"To break the fast and destroy the precepts, to slaughter chickens and pigs— The karma-mirror reflects this clearly; retribution is never in vain."
If one composes this sutra and paints its images, King Yama shall judge and release them,
and their offenses shall be extinguished. If there are good men or good women— whether bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās—
who prepare the *shengqi* (seven-day) fasts for the future life, making offerings to the Triple Gem twice every month and praying to the Ten Kings, they shall cultivate the practice known as *na*.
The petition was submitted to the Six Ministries. The youth Shan-ye submitted it to the officials of the Celestial Bureau and the Earthly Courts, who recorded it on their registers.

On the day his body arrived [at the courts], he was immediately assigned to a place of happiness and did not remain in the intermediate state for forty-nine days, nor did he await rescue by male or female relatives.
Once the ten kings had passed his case, if even one were missing from the assembly, he would be detained by that single king and left behind.

Even while suffering, one cannot attain birth [in the Pure Land] and is delayed for a year. For this reason, I exhort you to perform this essential task and pray for the karmic reward of rebirth there. The eulogy says:
The fourfold assembly shall cultivate harmony and practice at appointed times; providing offerings twice every ten days is the constant ritual.
Do not allow conditions to fail, for the merit would otherwise be slight; thus one may avoid becoming obstructed by the intermediate state (antarābhava) within the offices of the underworld.
At that time, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva, the Suffering-Relieving Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, and Sadāprarudita Bodhisattva...
The Bodhisattva Sāradvatīputra and the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha each returned through the light of their original radiance to the place where the Tathāgata was.
With one voice and in unison, they praised the World-Honored One, saying: "Out of compassion for ordinary beings, you have preached this wondrous Dharma, which uproots death and saves living beings.
They prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and said in praise:
With knees, chests, mouths, and brows pressed to the ground, the Bodhisattvas of the Six Radiances moved by profound compassion each praised him in unison:
"Diligently transform sentient beings without ever becoming weary.
At that time, the twenty-eight tiers of all the hell-wardens, King Yama, and the dark officials of the six realms prostrated themselves.

I make this vow: If there are members of the fourfold assembly—monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen—who transcribe this sutra or recite even a single verse from it, I shall deliver them from all suffering and distress, send them forth from the hells, and establish them in the heavenly realms, ensuring they do not linger or endure suffering for more than a single night. Praise says:
The officials of the underworld record [deeds], as does King Yama; The Buddhas propagate the sutras, and the fourfold assembly offers praise and exaltation.
If there are those who can uphold even a single verse, I shall send them all forth to the heavenly realm.
At that time, the Celestial Son Yama spoke this verse to the Buddha.
Homage to the Arhat. Sentient beings have many karmic sufferings; their saṃsāra has no fixed form, just like waves upon the water.
The King of Yama addressed the Buddha in verse, saying: "I take pity on sentient beings, for their sins and sufferings are many."
The six realms of saṃsāra have no fixed form; Arising and ceasing are like waves upon the water.
I pray that the wind of wisdom may blow, Carrying me across the river of the Dharma wheel. May its radiance illuminate the world, Passing through every place as it travels.
Universally rescuing sentient beings from suffering and subduing and gathering all māras, the Four Kings traverse the realms and proclaim the Buddha’s sūtras,
praising them thus:
“May the Buddha raise the wind of wisdom To waft us back to the ocean of Dharma and wash away the dust of delusion.”
The Four World-Protecting Kings made this vow together: "May these scriptures always be transmitted and widely circulated.
Ordinary people practice little goodness and mostly hold perverted views, believing in the heterodox. By upholding this sutra, one escapes hell; by copying it, one escapes calamities and ailments."
They transcend the hardships of the three realms and shall never again behold yakṣas. In their place of birth, they ascend to high positions; wealthy, noble, and long-lived.
It is praised thus:
"Ordinary people of evil karma possess feeble power of goodness; trusting in heterodox and inverted views, they enter Avīci."
If you seek wealth, happiness, long life for your family, and headship, transcribe this scripture and listen to it with a devoted heart;

recite this sutra with sincerity, for the Heavenly Kings will constantly record your deeds. If you wish to remain free from transgression and blame, do not kill living beings to sacrifice to the spirits.
For this reason, one enters hell. By recollecting the Buddha and reverently honoring the True Sutra, one should admonish oneself:
holding the vajra-sword in hand, sever the lineage of Māra. The eulogy says:
The karma of the three miserable realms is easily formed through the suffering of transgressions; all this is due to sacrificing living beings to worship the gods.
I pray that you grasp the true wisdom-sword of the Vajradhara, to sever and eliminate the demonic hordes and realize non-arising.
The Buddha practices an impartial mind, yet sentient beings lack this; their cultivation of merit is like a speck of dust, while the sins they commit are like mountain peaks.
If one desires to obtain a long life, one should cultivate and practice this sutra. It can eliminate the sufferings of hell and lead to rebirth in a noble and wealthy family.
Virtuous deities will constantly provide protection. The praise says:
Though their sins may be as vast as mountains and as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, and their merit as slight as the number of minute motes of dust,
they still receive the constant protection of benevolent deities. Those who have produced this sutra, recited it, and studied it,
even if they suddenly pass away at the end of their natural lifespan, will be constantly welcomed by the Heavenly Kings and received with flowers held out by Bodhisattvas.
Following one's mind, one goes to the Pure Land; through eight hundred billion births, one fulfills the practice and enters the city of Vajra-samādhi.
The praise says:
"If a person honors the Buddha and upholds this sutra, the Bodhisattva will personally go to welcome them at the time of death."
"Once you have perfected your practice in the Pure Land, you shall enter the Golden City as a future Buddha.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda, all the nāgas, spirits, and the eight classes of beings, as well as the various ministers and the Son of Heaven, Yama.
Lord of the Great Mountain, Director of Destiny, Director of Records, Great Deity of the Five Paths, and the officials of the hells;

O Heavenly Kings who traverse the realms, you should give rise to compassion and must not harbor arrogance. You should grant clemency to all sinners and to sons and daughters who practice filial piety, performing vegetarian feasts to cultivate merit, dedicating these acts to rescue the deceased and repay the kindness of their parents’ birth and upbringing.
By performing vegetarian feasts and creating sacred images at each of the seven-week intervals, one repays the debt owed to one’s father.
[May they] cause their mothers to attain rebirth in heaven. The praise says:
The Buddha addressed the great deities of Yama: "The karmic offenses of sentient beings are too numerous to fully describe;
one should perform meritorious deeds for the sake of repaying their kindness, teaching those who are deluded so that they may leave suffering behind and cross the ford of confusion."

The Dharma King Yama addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, we kings shall all dispatch messengers who ride black horses, carry black banners, and wear black robes to inspect the households of the deceased.
According to whatever merit they have performed, we shall issue certificates of release and extract the offenders from [the hells], not failing to fulfill our vows. He then offered this praise:
The various kings dispatch envoys to inspect the deceased; based on what meritorious deeds men and women have cultivated, they are released from the three miserable realms.
Thus they avoid passing through the dark regions and encountering bitter suffering.
When the first seven days have passed, King Qin Guang offers this praise:
In the first seven days, the intermediate bodies (*antarābhava*) of the deceased are driven along in throngs as numerous as dust motes;
they are first brought before King Qi (Qi-jian-dian), for whom none have ever crossed the ford of the Nai River.
When the second seven-day period has passed, they proceed to the first river, King Wang (Wang-zan). He praises them, saying:
On the second seven-day period, the deceased crosses the Nai River; thousands upon ten thousands of throngs wade through the river waves.
The Ox-Headed Guide leads the way, carrying a staff over his shoulder, while the driving ghost-soldiers hold pitchforks in their hands.
After the third seven-day period has passed, King Song praises [the deceased], saying:
The deceased undergoes three weeks of intense anxiety and distress; Only then do they realize that the path to the underworld is perilous and long.
Each is called by name to ascertain their location, As groups are driven along to the King of the Five Officials.
When the fourth seven-day period has passed, the King of the Five Officials offers this praise:
The scales of the Five Officials hang suspended in the void; On either side, two youths hold the complete registers of karma.
How could lightness or heaviness be according to one's own desires? High or low is determined by one’s own past causes and conditions.
After the fifth seven-day period has passed, King Yama praises them, saying:
On the thirty-fifth day, King Yama ceases his clamor; though the sinner’s heart harbors resentment and finds no satisfaction, he combs his hair and looks up at the karma-mirror.
Only then does he realize that the affairs of his past lives are clearly revealed.
When the sixth seven-day period has passed, he becomes a king. It is praised, saying:
The deceased lingers on the dark path for six or seven days, pressed by urgency as they sit upon their own deluded intent;
yet if one looks daily only toward the power of merit, heaven and hell lie within a mere moment.
When the seventh week has passed, one crosses the Great Mountain King. The praise says:
In the forty-nine days of the intermediate state (*antarābhava*), the subtle body (*manomaya-kāya*) seeks exclusively to reunite with parents and kinsmen;
at this time, one’s merit and karma remain undetermined, and it further depends upon what causes the sons and daughters create.

When the eight hundredth day has passed, King Samatā praises, saying: [The verse follows... *Note: The final line of the source text appears to be a concluding title or colophon indicating the end of a section.*
For a hundred days after the person has passed away, they remain in a state of great distress; their body is bound by shackles and galled by whips.
May men and women strive with effort to create merit, so that through compassion and wondrous goodness, they may behold the heavenly realm.
The Ninth Year: Passing Through the City Market, King. He praised, saying:

When one year has passed, suffering becomes even more bitter; though men and women cultivate the causes of merit through fasting and virtuous deeds, their transmigration through the six realms remains undetermined.
By creating scriptures and images of the Buddha, they emerge from the ford of delusion.
(Verse 10) When three years have passed, one becomes a Wheel-Turning King over the five paths. The eulogy says:
The latter three stages traversed are the opening of the ferry; good and evil depend solely upon the causes of one's meritorious karma.

Even for those who do not practice the good, there is still cause for concern within a thousand days; yet for those whose bodies undergo birth from the womb, production, death, or untimely demise, if they fully observe the Ten Observances (*daśa-śīla*), they shall be exempt from the ten evils. Released from these, they shall ascend to heaven. The eulogy says:
The suffering of the six realms within one body is vast and boundless; the ten evils and three miserable paths are not easily overcome.
Strive diligently to cultivate the merit of the fast, and the sins as numerous as the sands of the Ganges will naturally perish.
I shall constantly cause the four yakṣa kings to protect this sutra, ensuring it does not sink into oblivion. Thus it was praised:

May King Yama uphold the Dharma and propagate it widely; may he universally announce to the assembly of humans and devas that I shall cause the yakṣas to guard this site of practice in unison, so that it shall never be obscured but shall circulate forever.
I prostrate to the World-Honored One. As for the offenders in the hells, many have used the property of the Triple Gem; they undergo retribution amidst clamor and noise. May their consciousnesses...
Those who possess faith should admonish themselves with vigilance and must not offend the Triple Gem; the retribution for such karma is difficult to evade.
Those who encounter this sutra should practice and study it. The Praise says:
Those who seek to dwell in peace and happiness among humans and devas must never encroach upon the property of the Triple Gem.
Once it falls into the various hells of the dark realm, one will suffer amidst clamorous cries for years on end, unaware of the passing time.
At that moment, King Yama, the Lord of Dharma, leaped for joy and prostrated at the Buddha’s feet; then, withdrawing to sit to one side, he addressed the Buddha.
This sutra is titled *The Sutra on Receiving the Prediction for the Fourfold Assembly from King Yama: Preparing for Rebirth in the Pure Land*.
You should circulate it throughout the realm and practice according to its teachings. Praise says:
King Yama withdrew to sit and listen with single-minded attention.

The Buddha again earnestly entrusted this sutra, titled "The Teaching on Preparing for Rebirth through the Seven-Day Rite," and exhorted you, along with the fourfold assembly, to propagate and practice it widely.
The Buddha spoke the *Sutra on King Yama’s Prophecy to the Fourfold Assembly: Preparing for Rebirth through the Seven-Day Rite for Birth in the Pure Land*, universally encouraging all.
There is a cause. Having cultivated merit in advance, one resolves the mind to take refuge in the Buddha, wishing to bring rest to saṃsāra. Two Verses of Praise.
First Verse:
This single body is fragile and precarious like a wind lamp; Two mice, through their predatory gnawing, have bitten the well-rope.
If one does not construct a bridge or raft to cross the sea of suffering, by what means can one hope for transcendence?
Second, returning to the Buddha to cultivate the mind, it is said in praise:
"This person is deluded not to build a boat or bridge; only when encountering peril and distress will you finally realize it."
If you realize that a hundred years pass in the snap of a finger, do not delay in practicing the fasts and listening to the Dharma.
The Buddha spoke the *Sutra on the Preemptive Cultivation for the Ten Kings and the Seven Generations*;

this scripture reveals the manifestation of the scales of judgment. The Great Sage responds to capacities, while the Compassionate King holds the mirror and the scale; he vows to exhaust the delusions of all beings.
Lun has thus realized Bodhi. His profound and vast vows are sublime and exhaustive.

When ordinary beings currently dwell in the realm of darkness, his true body surely descends among those suffering classes to provide ultimate salvation for the submerged multitudes, uprooting their pain and bestowing joy; nothing can surpass this.
The practitioner [Name] widely exhorted both the monastic and lay communities to reverently complete the ritual protocols for making offerings. May you adorn yourself with these and peruse them.
May we be blessed by the profound protection of the unseen, with our present merit, fortune, and longevity increasing; may the souls of those from past generations ascend to realms of bliss;
and may we pray for the eternal prosperity of the state’s mandate and that the people roam in a city of abundance—how fortunate we are to be thus!
Recorded on the [blank] day of the sixth month in the fifth year of the Chenghua era.
